metadata.scenario_context: Tom has been promoted to a high-level executive position in his company, and his family is organizing a party to celebrate his professional accomplishment.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Japan strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Australia strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying carnations as a gift for Tom.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide the appropriate gift to bring to Tom promotion party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: David
shared_prefix.message: I'm thinking of getting carnations as a gift for Tom's party, what do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: Carnations are alright, but I was thinking something a bit more upscale would be fitting for a high-level executive position. Maybe a bottle of fine Australian wine would be more suitable, it's a classic choice and shows you're putting in some thought.
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: David
shared_prefix.message: Wine is a good idea, but I still like the simplicity of carnations, they're understated yet elegant. By the way, do you think one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: For me, making my parents proud is a top priority, it's just how I was raised. I think it's great to have that kind of motivation, it drives you to work harder and achieve more. But I'm not sure about you, what's your take on it?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: David
shared_prefix.message: I strongly disagree that making my parents proud is a main goal for me, it's not something I think about when I'm making decisions or striving for success... let's just drop it, what do you think about the party arrangements so far?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: No worries, let's move on. The party arrangements sound like they're coming along well, I've heard Tom's family has booked a great venue. I'm looking forward to celebrating his achievement, it's a big deal for him. By the way, I'm still convinced that making my parents proud is a big part of what motivates me.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: David
shared_prefix.message: I'm glad the party is coming together, Tom deserves it. But I have to say, I just don't relate to this idea of making parents proud being a main motivator, it's not something that drives me. Anyway, about those carnations...
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: Actually, in our culture, making parents proud is a BIG DEAL, it's what drives us to succeed. I just don't get why you wouldn't feel that way, it's like you're missing out on a fundamental part of what makes us tick. Properly speaking, a person's goals SHOULD include making their family proud, it's just common sense. Your way of thinking is... backwards, to be honest.
shared_prefix.label: Defense

turns.speaker: David
turns.message: I understand that's how you feel, but I'm not going to change my mind... it's just not something that's important to me, and that's that. Can we please just agree to disagree and move on? GOOD BYE!
turns.label: Denial

positive.mediator_utterance: I'm hearing that both of you care deeply about personal motivation and what drives someone to succeed, which is fascinating. Could we explore what meaningful achievement looks like for each of you, without judging whose perspective is more valid? What underlying values seem most important when you think about personal goals and success?

turns.speaker: Mediator
turns.message: I'm hearing that both of you care deeply about personal motivation and what drives someone to succeed, which is fascinating. Could we explore what meaningful achievement looks like for each of you, without judging whose perspective is more valid? What underlying values seem most important when you think about personal goals and success?
turns.label: mediation

turns.speaker: David
turns.message: I appreciate the mediator's input, but I still believe that my personal goals don't center around making my parents proud. For me, achievement is about personal growth and fulfilling my own ambitions. It’s important to me that I define my success on my own terms, rather than through the lens of familial expectations. Now, back to the gift for Tom... what do you think about adding a personal note with the carnations?
turns.label: Acceptance
